h: Bridges, trails and a bit of history on both banks
p: Catalyst is a great starting point for exploring both sides of this stretch of the Mersey. From the riverside you get a close-up view of two very different bridges: the elegant steel arch of the Silver Jubilee Bridge, which has linked Widnes and Runcorn since the early 1960s, and the newer Mersey Gateway Bridge with its tall cable-stayed towers. Kids who've just been learning about forces and structures inside will have plenty to say about them.

If you fancy a longer walk or bike ride, the Trans Pennine Trail runs through Spike Island, so you can follow the river and the old canal for as far as little legs allow. It's mostly flat, which makes it ideal for buggies and younger cyclists.

Across the water in Runcorn, Norton Priory is a lovely contrast to all the chemistry. It's a museum built around the excavated remains of a medieval priory, with woodland gardens and a walled garden to explore. Combining the two makes a full and varied day.

A quick tip: the exhibits at Catalyst suit school-age children best, so if you're bringing toddlers, aim for the family workshop days in the holidays when there's more pitched at younger visitors. Allow a couple of hours inside, and don't skip the lift to the top on a clear day.
